reasons: Direction is correct: Section 7.2 runs the MFN against us (Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given any other technology supplier), which is the exact pattern the rule targets; no Vendor-granted MFN is being removed.

Clause fails the fallback on material terms — no defined product/service, no 12-month limit, no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so 'deviation' rather than 'compliant at fallback' is the right classification, and it matches the stated walk-away formulation.
Redline is the minimal edit that reaches the preferred position: full deletion of p0027, exactly as the redline guidance directs (delete the Customer-side obligation).

Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, first-person plural and concise; it cites the playbook position, notes the internal inconsistency with Section 12.3, and preserves willingness to accept MFN pricing in our favour. High changed-character ratio is expected and appropriate for a deletion remedy.
